newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa Cargo trucks to overcome French ban.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa Cargo trucks to overcome French ban.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG said it would have to re-schedule its international truck services due to a planned weekend truck ban in France.
From March 24, truckers transporting airfreight from, to or through France will face a 24-hour driving ban starting Saturdays at 2200 local time (2100 GMT).
Truckers will have to apply individually for exemptions unless carrying perishable goods, animals or printed matter.
Hans Driedger, Lufthansa Cargo general manager for capacity planning and procedures, said: "This new ruling increases the impression that European trucking is going towards a weekend ban."
"But the consequences are not dramatic. We will partly lose our flexibility and will have to change some route frequencies."
This could involve switching Sunday departures to the following day and tightening up on journey times, he indicated.
The French truck ban would affect not only Lufthansa Cargo but other companies operating between Germany and France at weekends, he added. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
